slides.1.title: 🏛️ Wines of the Eternal City
slides.1.content:
Lazio is home to Rome (Roma), and its wine history reaches back to ancient Roman times. It is known for Frascati and for the legend of Est! Est!! Est!!! di Montefiascone.

Lazio is mainly white (about 70% white grapes), largely supplying Rome’s huge restaurant trade, and is one of Italy’s oldest wine regions.

slides.3.title: 🍇 Frascati DOCG — The Star of Lazio
slides.3.content:
🏰 The white wine of the Roman hills

Frascati comes from the volcanic hills of the Castelli Romani south-east of Rome and is the most common white in Roman restaurants — affordable and easy to drink. Superiore was promoted to DOCG in 2011.

🍇 Grapes

  • Malvasia Bianca di Candia and/or Malvasia del Lazio: min. 70%
  • Remaining max. 30%: Bombino Bianco, Bellone, Trebbiano Toscano, Trebbiano Giallo, Greco Bianco

🍷 Styles

Secco (dry): the main version

White flowers, green apple, almond, minerality

Superiore DOCG: lower yields and higher alcohol; Riserva min. 12 months’ ageing

More depth, body and character

Cannellino DOCG: a sweet wine from the same area as Frascati DOC

Traditionally made from botrytised grapes, now mostly late-harvested (botrytis is rare); delicate and sweet, balanced by acidity

⚠️ Quality guide

Mass production of cheap wine once damaged its reputation. Quality-focused producers have been raising standards in recent years.

What to look for:

  • Frascati Superiore DOCG
  • Small quality-focused producers
  • Organic certification, sur lie ageing
slides.4.title: 📖 Est! Est!! Est!!! di Montefiascone DOC
slides.4.content:
📜 A 12th-century legend: a German bishop travelling to Rome sent his servant Martin ahead, telling him to mark inns with good wine with “Est” (it is here!). Martin was so impressed in Montefiascone that he wrote “Est!!!” three times — and the bishop reputedly stayed there until his death. The legend is more famous than the wine itself.

🍋 Est! Est!! Est!!! di Montefiascone DOC

Grapes: mostly Trebbiano Toscano, with smaller amounts of Trebbiano Giallo, Malvasia del Lazio and/or Malvasia Bianca Lunga

Area: Montefiascone lies on Lake Bolsena (northern Lazio); the appellation surrounds the whole lake

Style: fresh, light, easy-drinking; lemon, green apple, white flowers, almond

Key facts: Lazio’s historic white; became Lazio’s first DOC in 1966; white wine only

Pairing: lake fish, mussels, fried salt cod, white meats
slides.5.title: 🍷 Cesanese Red Wines
slides.5.content:
Cesanese is Lazio’s most important red grape, grown mainly in the Ciociaria area south-east of Rome, home of Lazio’s only red DOCG. Cesanese is in fact two genetically distinct varieties: the higher-quality Cesanese d’Affile (native to the town of Affile), whose plantings are increasing, and Cesanese Comune, historically the more widely planted.

🏆 Cesanese del Piglio DOCG

Lazio’s only red DOCG

Promoted: DOCG in 2008

Location: town of Piglio (60 km south-east of Rome)

Grapes: min. 90% Cesanese Comune and/or Cesanese d’Affile; also Superiore and Superiore Riserva

Style: aromatic, well structured, fruit-led, often oak-aged

Flavours: cherry, strawberry, violet, spice, herbs

Pairing: grilled lamb chops, wild-boar ragù, aged Pecorino

Drinking window: 5-15 years

🍷 Cesanese di Olevano Romano DOC

Traditional DOC

Location: the small town of Olevano Romano

Grapes: Cesanese (85%+)

Style: traditional; can be dry or off-dry

Types: Secco, Amabile (off-dry), Dolce (sweet)

Key facts: easier-drinking than Piglio DOCG, varied styles, affordable

Pairing: meat-sauce pasta, pizza, stews

Drinking window: now - 5 years
slides.6.title: 📜 Lazio Appellations and Grapes in Full (IWS Course Material)
slides.6.content:
🏆 Frascati’s three appellations

Area: the volcanic soils of the Castelli Romani south-east of Rome; Frascati is the historic white of Rome and Lazio and the region’s best-known wine. Min. 70% Malvasia Bianca di Candia and/or Malvasia del Lazio, max. 30% Bombino Bianco, Bellone, Trebbiano Toscano, Trebbiano Giallo, Greco Bianco.

Frascati DOC: simple, light and fresh; mostly secco, but sweeter styles such as abboccato and amabile are also allowed. Frascati Superiore DOCG: stricter rules (lower yields, higher alcohol), with more depth and character than the DOC; Riserva min. 12 months’ ageing. Cannellino di Frascati DOCG: a sweet wine from the same area as Frascati DOC, traditionally from botrytised grapes, now mostly late-harvested; delicate and sweet, balanced by acidity.

🍷 Cesanese’s three appellations

Grape: Cesanese is Lazio’s most important native red grape and is in fact two genetically distinct varieties — the higher-quality Cesanese d’Affile, whose plantings are increasing, and the historically more common Cesanese Comune.

Cesanese del Piglio DOCG (Lazio’s only red DOCG): min. 90% Cesanese Comune and/or d’Affile, with Superiore and Superiore Riserva; aromatic, well structured, fruit-led, often oak-aged. Cesanese di Olevano Romano DOC, and Cesanese di Affile DOC (a small area around the town of Affile, east of Rome; min. 90% Cesanese d’Affile).

📖 Est! Est!! Est!!! di Montefiascone DOC

Lazio’s historic white, which became Lazio’s first DOC in 1966; Montefiascone lies on Lake Bolsena and the appellation surrounds the lake. White only, mostly Trebbiano Toscano with smaller amounts of Trebbiano Giallo, Malvasia del Lazio and/or Malvasia Bianca Lunga.

🍇 Grape profile

White grapes account for about 70%, mainly Trebbiano and Malvasia: Malvasia Bianca di Candia has the largest area under vine; Malvasia del Lazio (Puntinata) is considered native and of higher quality. Cesanese and Merlot represent the reds, with Merlot the most planted red grape. Note: most of the cross-border Orvieto DOC’s area and production lies in Umbria, not Lazio.
slides.7.title: 🌋 The Influence of Volcanic Soils
slides.7.content:
🌋 Extinct volcanoes shape the soul of Lazio’s wines: Lazio’s vineyards lie largely around ancient volcanoes such as the Colli Albani. Mineral-rich volcanic soils give the wines a distinctive savoury note and complexity, and are at the heart of the Frascati style.

🌋

Volcanic ash soil (Pozzolana)

  • Properties: high porosity, excellent drainage, rich in trace minerals
  • Where: the Marino and Colli Albani core zones
  • Contribution: strong minerality, white flowers, elegant acidity
🪨

Tuff (Tufo)

  • Properties: compacted volcanic debris, calcium-cemented, well aerated
  • Where: the core soil of Frascati and Zagarolo
  • Contribution: structural complexity, ageing potential, savoury flavours

🔑 Four key effects of volcanic soils on wine

💎 Mineral-rich

Volcanic soils are rich in minerals, giving pronounced minerality and complexity

💧 Good drainage

Porous soils drain well, so vine roots grow deep and draw on deeper minerals

🌡️ Temperature regulation

Dark volcanic soils absorb heat by day and release it at night, moderating the diurnal range

🍇 Distinctive flavour

They bring smoky, mineral and savoury characters
slides.8.title: 🍇 Other Lazio DOCs
slides.8.content:
Marino DOC

Grapes: Malvasia + Trebbiano

Style: aromatic, white flowers, honeysuckle, fresh minerality

Key facts: Frascati’s aromatic neighbour, at higher elevation (300-500 m) and more affordable

Castelli Romani DOC

White: Malvasia + Trebbiano (fresh, easy-drinking)

Red: Cesanese, Sangiovese, Merlot

Key facts: covers the whole area, the most blending freedom, the everyday choice

Colli Albani DOC

Grapes: Malvasia + Trebbiano

Style: apple, pear, almond, rounded body

Key facts: whites from around Lake Albano, ideal for everyday meals

Cannellino di Frascati DOCG

Production: traditionally from botrytised grapes, now mostly late-harvested

Style: honey, apricot, white flowers; an elegant sweet wine

Key facts: a sweet DOCG from the same area as Frascati DOC, delicate and sweet, balanced by acidity
slides.9.title: 🍽️ Roman Cuisine and Wine Pairing
slides.9.content:
🍝 Rome’s four classic pastas

Lazio’s wines mainly serve Rome’s traditional cuisine; the acidity and minerality of the whites cut through fat and lift the dishes.

🥚 Carbonara

  • Ingredients: egg yolk, Pecorino Romano, guanciale, black pepper
  • ✅ Frascati Superiore (acidity cuts the richness of the yolk)
  • ✅ Marino DOC (fresh minerality)

🍅 Amatriciana

  • Ingredients: tomato, guanciale, Pecorino Romano, chilli
  • ✅ Cesanese del Piglio (red fruit echoes the tomato)
  • ✅ Castelli Romani Rosso

🧀 Cacio e Pepe

  • Ingredients: Pecorino Romano, black pepper, pasta water
  • ✅ Frascati (fresh and cleansing)
  • ✅ Est! Est!! Est!!! (light and easy-drinking)

🥓 Gricia

  • Ingredients: guanciale, Pecorino Romano, black pepper
  • ✅ Frascati Superiore
  • ✅ Cesanese di Olevano Romano Secco
slides.10.title: 🏛️ History: From Ancient Rome to the Papal States (IWS Course Material)
slides.10.content:
🏛️ Rome’s hinterland: Etruscans to the north, Greek colonies to the south; as the Latini rose they absorbed Greek culture, and wine became central to Roman society. The most celebrated wine of imperial times, Falernian, came from neighbouring northern Campania.

Antiquity

🏺 Etruscans, Greeks and the Latini

The north was Etruscan, the south had Greek colonies; around 300 BCE the Latini grew powerful and expanded across the peninsula, and through contact with the Greeks in the south they absorbed their culture, mythology and regard for wine.

Roman Empire

🍇 Wine at the heart of Roman civilisation

The Romans developed more sophisticated viticulture and spread it across western Europe as the empire expanded; planting vineyards became a tool of colonisation.

Middle Ages

⛪ Monasteries and the Papal States

After the fall of the Roman Empire in 476 AD came turmoil; viticulture survived and progressed in the monasteries, and wine became central to Christianity. The Papal States, with Rome as capital, were founded in 756; the papacy moved to Avignon in 1309 and returned to Rome in 1377.

Modern era

🏰 The Vatican and the Castelli Romani

Vatican City became a sovereign state in 1929. The volcanic Castelli Romani hills south-east of Rome were long a summer retreat for popes and nobles; the papal summer residence, Castel Gandolfo, is here.

Appellations

📜 From 1966: DOC and DOCG

In 1966 Est! Est!! Est!!! di Montefiascone became Lazio’s first DOC, and Frascati became a DOC the same year; Cesanese del Piglio was promoted to DOCG in 2008, Frascati Superiore and Cannellino di Frascati in 2011.

slides.11.title: 🌋 Topography, Climate, Soils and Volcanic Lakes (IWS Course Material)
slides.11.content:
⛰️ Over 50% of Lazio is hills, stretching from the Central Apennines to the coast; the climate is Mediterranean on the coast and becomes increasingly continental eastwards into the hills and mountains.

🌋

Extremely diverse soils

  • Volcanic: from the Volsini volcanoes in the north to the Colli Albani south-east of Rome
  • Limestone: in the south
  • Sandy clay: on the coast and along the Tevere
☀️

Climate

  • Coast: Mediterranean
  • Inland: increasingly continental eastwards into the hills and mountains
  • Topography: mainly hills, plus the coastal plains of the Maremma Laziale and Agro Pontino

slides.12.title: 🍇 The Malvasia Family Decoded
slides.12.content:
🍇 Lazio’s Malvasias and other white grapes

Understanding the diversity

  • “Malvasia” is a collective name for several genetically distinct varieties, not a single grape
  • Lazio is mainly white (about 70%), led by Trebbiano and Malvasia, with many minor white grapes
  • Frascati requires min. 70% Malvasia Bianca di Candia and/or Malvasia del Lazio

Other varieties

  • White: Trebbiano Toscano, Trebbiano Giallo, Bellone, Bombino Bianco, Greco Bianco, Grechetto, Moscato di Terracina
  • Red: Cesanese, Merlot (the most planted red), Sangiovese, Montepulciano, Aleatico, Nero Buono

🍷 Three key white grapes compared

Malvasia Bianca di Candia

The variety with the largest area under vine in Lazio

Vigorous and high-yielding; neutral wines with medium aromas, medium acidity, full body and high alcohol

Role: the volume workhorse

Malvasia del Lazio (Puntinata)

Considered native to Lazio, with dark specks on its skins (puntinata = “dotted”); a natural cross of Muscat of Alexandria and Schiava Grossa

Higher quality than Malvasia Bianca di Candia; lightly aromatic, round and full, prone to botrytis

Role: the quality grape

Trebbiano Toscano

The main grape of Est! Est!! Est!!!

Green apple, lemon, freshness

Role: structure

Key to winemaking: top Frascati Superiore is often built on Malvasia del Lazio, with cool fermentation and lees ageing for more complexity; since Malvasia del Lazio is prone to botrytis, it also suits sweet Cannellino.
slides.13.title: 🍷 Label Example: Roma DOC Malvasia Puntinata
slides.13.caption: Tenuta San Leo “Commodo” Roma DOC Malvasia Puntinata — the label states the single variety Malvasia Puntinata (i.e. Malvasia del Lazio); Roma DOC was created in 2011 and covers the greater Rome area.
slides.14.title: 🍶 Traditional vs Modern Winemaking
slides.14.content:
⚗️ The quality revolution: before the 1990s Frascati was cheap bulk wine (€3-5 a bottle). Since the 2000s, quality-focused producers have cut yields and adopted modern winemaking, and the quality of top Frascati Superiore DOCG has risen markedly.

🏺 Traditional methods (1950-1990)

  • Harvest: machine-harvested, yields of 12-14 t/ha
  • Fermentation: commercial yeasts, fast (5-7 days) at 18-22°C
  • Vessels: large stainless-steel tanks (20,000-50,000 L)
  • Ageing: no lees contact, bottled after 3-4 months
  • Style: light, neutral, little complexity

🔬 Modern quality methods (2000-today)

  • Harvest: hand-picked in several passes, yields of 6-8 t/ha
  • Fermentation: wild or selected yeasts, slow (15-18 days) at 12-16°C
  • Vessels: small stainless-steel tanks (500-2,000 L) or concrete eggs
  • Ageing: sur lie for 6-12 months with regular bâtonnage
  • Style: complex and mineral, with ageing potential

🍶 How flavours evolve with sur lie ageing

🍋
3 months

First creamy texture, fresh fruit

→
🍞
6 months

Toast, yeast, vanilla

→
🥜
9 months

Nuts, honey, depth

→
💎
12 months

Smoke and minerality integrate; ageing potential emerges
slides.15.title: 🏰 Castelli Romani: The 4 Core DOCs
slides.15.content:
🏰 The Castelli Romani (Roman castles) are volcanic hills 25-40 km south-east of Rome, around the Colli Albani volcanic complex. From the Middle Ages to the Renaissance they were a summer retreat for popes and nobles, who built many castles; the volcanic soils produce Malvasia-based whites.

🏆 Frascati DOC (1966) / DOCG (2011)

Soil: volcanic, tuff (tufo)

White flowers, minerality, nuts; the DOCG is internationally known, €6-35

Producers: Castel de Paolis, Poggio Le Volpi, Fontana Candida

🌿 Marino DOC (1970)

Soil: volcanic ash + pozzolana

Aromatic: white flowers, honeysuckle, marked minerality, €7-14

Key facts: Frascati’s higher-altitude aromatic neighbour, more affordable

🌅 Colli Albani DOC (1970)

Soil: volcanic + tuff

Rounded: apple, pear, almond; an everyday choice, €6-12

Key facts: around Lake Albano, soft and easy-drinking

🍷 Velletri DOC (1972)

Soil: volcanic

White + red: fruit-led whites; reds (Sangiovese + Montepulciano) that can age, €7-18

Key facts: the only Castelli Romani appellation notable for both white and red

🏰 Montecompatri Colonna DOC (1973)

Soil: volcanic ash

Style: traditional, soft apricot; off-dry Amabile versions are common, €7-13

🍋 Zagarolo DOC (1973)

Soil: mainly tuff

Style: fresh, citrus, green apple, savoury; best drunk young, €6-11
slides.16.title: 🏆 The Rise of Lazio’s Quality Producers
slides.16.content:
🍷 From cheap bulk wine to a quality revolution: in the 1990s Lazio wine was at a low ebb (€3-5 a bottle); from the 2000s innovative producers cut yields and revived native grapes such as Cesanese and Bellone. Quality has risen markedly and is drawing international attention.

CP

est. 1985

Castel de Paolis 🏆

Standing: a pioneer of quality Frascati and a driver of Lazio’s modern winemaking revolution

Location: Grottaferrata, Frascati; 13 ha; 300-350 m

Hallmarks: old-vine Malvasia del Lazio, lees ageing, also international varieties

• Frascati Superiore “Campo Vecchio”: €24 (old vines, 10 months sur lie)

• “Vigna Adriana” IGT: €32 (Malvasia del Lazio + Viognier)

Tip: Campo Vecchio shows its best mineral and honeyed layers at 5-8 years

SM

est. 1933

Sergio Mottura 🌿

Standing: the ultimate interpreter of Grechetto, a legendary estate of northern Lazio

Location: Civitella d’Agliano, Viterbo; 30 ha; 45-year-old vines

Hallmarks: organic farming; the benchmark for Grechetto in northern Lazio

• “Poggio della Costa” Grechetto: €18 (fresh, mineral entry level)

• “Latour a Civitella” Grechetto: €40 (top wine, long ageing potential)

Note: the top wine needs 5-10 years to open fully and show honeyed, smoky complexity

Poggio Le Volpi 🔬

📍 Monte Porzio Catone; 55 ha

Works with the University of Rome’s agriculture faculty on scientific study of volcanic soils

Frascati Superiore: €16

Frascati Superiore Riserva: €26

Ageing: 3-6 years

Fontana Candida 🌍

📍 Monte Porzio Catone; 100 ha

One of the best-known Frascati brands internationally

Frascati DOC: €8

Superiore “Santa Teresa”: €22

Ageing: 2-5 years

The Cori area 🌱

📍 Latina province; Cori DOC

Producers such as Marco Carpineti and Cincinnato are reviving the ancient varieties Bellone and Nero Buono

Nero Buono: €15-25

Bellone: €12-25

Ageing: 2-8 years

📍 Le Ferriere, Latina; 180 ha

Pioneering on reclaimed marshland in the Agro Pontino, exploring southern Lazio’s potential
